text:
Lucas Raymond had 9 points in 5 games for Sweden at the Olympics in February, and he remains the Red Wings' engine. He has 16 points in 18 games, 9 of them on the power play, while playing just over 20 minutes a night.

The trouble is around him. Detroit lost four of its last five games, and Raymond has gone two straight without a point. His own process is fine: his chances are up to 1.19 expected goals per 60 from 0.78 last season, and his shot ranks in the 96th percentile for top speed by NHL EDGE. He has 6 goals on 7.2 expected, a little short, and the Wings have scored 4.2 fewer goals than their chances with him on the ice.

Last season Evolving-Hockey had him 26th among 401 forwards in wins above replacement, mostly from even-strength offense, while facing the other team's best. Nothing here says that player has gone anywhere. If the bounces come back his way, the points will follow, and Detroit needs them soon.
headline: Raymond is producing on a team that is sliding
